message.content:
In blackjack an **ace** is special because its point value isn’t fixed—it can represent either *one* or *eleven*, whichever benefits your hand most without causing a bust.

### How it works

| Situation | Value used |
|-----------|------------|
| If treating the ace as 11 keeps the total ≤ 21 → **use 11** (the “soft” total). |
| If using 11 would make the hand > 21 → **downgrade to 1** so you don’t bust (“hard” total). |

> *Example:*  
> • Hand: A♠ + 7♦ → Total could be 8 or 18. Since 18 ≤ 21 we usually keep it at 18 (a soft‑18).  
> • Hand: A♥ + K♣ + 5♦ → Using 11 gives 26 (bust), so we count the ace as 1 → total = 16.

### Why this matters

- An ace counted as 11 creates a **“soft” hand**, which can still improve when drawing another card (e.g., soft‑17 can become 18, 19… up to 27 before busting).  
- Once the ace has been forced down to 1, the hand becomes **hard**—no further improvement possible from the same ace.

So the core rule: **An ace counts as eleven unless doing so would cause the hand’s total to exceed twenty‑one, in which case it counts as one.**
